01 — Abstract

What is Grokking?

Grokking is a striking phenomenon where a neural network first memorizes its training data — achieving near-perfect training accuracy almost immediately — then appears to stagnate for thousands of epochs before suddenly generalizing to unseen examples.

This project replicates and mechanistically analyzes grokking on modular arithmetic tasks, uncovering why generalization happens at all — through Fourier feature emergence, phase decomposition, and reverse-engineered algorithmic circuits.

We train a 2-layer transformer on (a + b) mod 67 and (a × b) mod 67, replicating Power et al. (2022). Training memorizes immediately but validation accuracy lags by ~10,750 epochs before grokking occurs. We show that this delay corresponds to the slow emergence of a sparse Fourier basis (ω ∈ {4, 6, 26, 27} for addition) in the model's weights. A three-phase decomposition — memorisation, circuit formation, and cleanup — fully explains the trajectory. We further demonstrate that grokking delay decreases sharply with training data fraction, and that co-grokking across addition and multiplication tasks occurs within a gap of just 1,800 epochs.

02 — Results & Plots

Key Findings

Six experiments document the full picture of grokking — from the core delay and loss curves through Fourier feature emergence, phase decomposition, and co-grokking across tasks.

🔍 click to zoom
Part 1 — Grokking: (a + b) mod 67 Training accuracy saturates near epoch ~500; validation accuracy remains near 0% until grokking at epoch 10,750. The log-scale loss plot (right) confirms the validation loss collapses sharply at the same point — a ~10,000 epoch delay between memorization and generalization.
🔍 click to zoom
Part 2 — Fourier Features: Addition (a + b, p=67) After grokking, embedding DFT power concentrates at ω ∈ {4, 6, 26, 27} — confirming a sparse Fourier basis. MLP neurons show the same dominant frequencies, validating end-to-end Fourier feature computation.
🔍 click to zoom
Part 2 — Fourier Features: Multiplication (a × b, p=67) The multiplication task learns a different sparse basis: ω ∈ {11, 21, 33}. Unlike addition, the embedding DFT shows a flatter spectrum — the circuit relies more heavily on the attention mechanism to implement the discrete-log isomorphism.
🔍 click to zoom
Part 3 — Three-Phase Grokking Decomposition (grokked @ ep 10,750) ① Memorisation (~0–500 ep): training accuracy → 100%, validation flat, loss drops, weight norm spikes.
② Circuit Formation (~500–10,750 ep): weight norm decays steadily as the Fourier circuit gradually displaces the memorization solution.
③ Cleanup (10,750+ ep): validation accuracy jumps to 100%, weight norm collapses to near zero — only the compact generalizing circuit survives.
🔍 click to zoom
Part 4 — Epochs Until Generalisation vs. Training Data Fraction (p=67) At 10%, 20%, 30% training data: no grokking within 15,000 epochs (✕). At 40%: grokking at ep 8,100. 50%→2,475  |  60%→1,350  |  70%→600  |  80%→525  |  90%→225. More training data dramatically compresses the generalization delay.
🔍 click to zoom
Part 5 — Algorithm Reverse-Engineering: (a × b) mod 67 via Discrete Logarithm The model learns the group isomorphism (ℤ₆₇*, ×) ≅ (ℤ₆₆, +). Panel A: token embeddings cluster by discrete-log index. Panel B: embedding norms are uniform across tokens. Panel C: DFT lives in ℤ₆₆ (not ℤ₆₇) — the model's algebraic fingerprint. Panel D: cosine similarity between embeddings correlates with |ind_g(a) − ind_g(b)|.
🔍 click to zoom
Part 6 — Co-Grokking: Addition + Multiplication on p=67 Training both tasks simultaneously, addition groks at ep 31,150 and multiplication at ep 32,950 — a gap of only 1,800 epochs. Panel D shows two sharp weight-norm drops at each grokking event, consistent with shared circuit reuse accelerating generalization on the second task.
03 — How to Run

Reproducing the Experiments

All experiments are in grokking_project.py. Requires Python 3.10+ and PyTorch.

1
Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/shahilrahman46-oss/Grokking.git
cd Grokking
2
Install dependencies
pip install torch matplotlib numpy
3
Run all experiments
python grokking_project.py
4
View outputs
# Plots saved automatically:
part1_grokking.png        # Accuracy + loss curves
part2_fourier.png         # Fourier features — addition
part2_fourier_mul.png     # Fourier features — multiplication
part3_phases.png          # Three-phase decomposition
part4_fraction_sweep.png  # Data fraction ablation
part5_algorithm.png       # Algorithm reverse-engineering
part6_cogrokking.png      # Co-grokking Add + Mul
